subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose anonymous Talk activity to plugins

question: Should plugins ever receive process-wide Talk activity, and if so which trusted operator or registry capability—not the plugin’s own manifest—authorizes that cross-session observation?
rationale: The patch can mechanically enforce an approved capability, but maintainers must decide whether a global activity feed is an acceptable Plugin SDK contract or whether only owner-scoped activity should exist.

options.title: Use owner-scoped observation
options.body: Restrict activity events to Talk sessions opened or owned by the calling plugin, avoiding a new cross-session entitlement.

options.title: Define a trusted global capability
options.body: Keep process-wide observation only after adding a registry- or operator-controlled capability with explicit approval, documentation, and focused authorization tests.

options.title: Pause the public API
options.body: Defer this SDK surface until the plugin trust model for cross-session voice metadata is agreed.

recommendation.title: Use owner-scoped observation
recommendation.body: Restrict activity events to Talk sessions opened or owned by the calling plugin, avoiding a new cross-session entitlement.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the recent contributor for the adjacent Talk session architecture and current Plugin SDK proposal, while the final trust-model choice remains a maintainer decision.
